content: SAFETY GUIDELINES FOR RICE STRAW HANDLING: Always wear protective gloves when handling rice straw to prevent cuts from sharp edges. Use dust masks to avoid inhaling particles. Store in dry areas to prevent mold growth. When burning (where permitted), ensure proper ventilation and fire safety measures. Avoid handling wet straw as it can harbor harmful bacteria. Keep straw away from electrical equipment to prevent fire hazards.

SAFETY GUIDELINES FOR CORN HUSK HANDLING: Wear gloves to prevent skin irritation from rough husk fibers. Ensure husks are properly dried before storage to prevent mold and pest infestation. When processing for handicrafts, use sharp tools carefully and maintain good lighting. Store in ventilated areas to prevent moisture buildup. Check for signs of fungal growth before use. Avoid inhaling dust particles during processing.

SAFETY GUIDELINES FOR WHEAT STRAW HANDLING: Use protective equipment including gloves, long sleeves, and eye protection. Wheat straw can cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals. Ensure proper ventilation when working in enclosed spaces. Store in dry conditions to prevent spontaneous combustion. Be aware of fire hazards, especially during dry seasons. When using as animal bedding, check for mold or contamination that could harm livestock.

SAFETY GUIDELINES FOR SUGARCANE BAGASSE HANDLING: Wear respiratory protection as bagasse dust can cause lung irritation. Use gloves and protective clothing to prevent skin contact with processing chemicals. Ensure proper ventilation in storage areas as bagasse can generate heat and gases during decomposition. Be cautious of fire hazards as dry bagasse is highly flammable. When using chemicals for processing, follow proper handling and disposal procedures.

SAFETY GUIDELINES FOR COCONUT COIR HANDLING: Wear gloves to protect hands from rough fibers and potential splinters. Use dust masks when processing dry coir to avoid inhaling particles. Ensure coir is properly cleaned and free from contaminants before use. Store in dry, well-ventilated areas to prevent mold growth. When soaking coir, use clean water and change regularly to prevent bacterial growth. Be aware that wet coir can be heavy and may cause back strain during handling.
